Apparently this game can randomly spawn enemies on top of the player. Worst part is that the dev confirmed that as an intentional design choice. The ensuing bs deaths simply weren't worth my time. EDIT: Everyone is missing my point, so I'm making it clear: I'm not giving a negative review over my slow reaction speed. (Dev's 200ms argument only applies when user is aware of what to react to, and that time worsens on higher cognitive load.) This problem is about going against the standard player expectation of first few seconds of the beginning of a level being safe, and the game doesn't warn you about it. I only became aware of spawn sniping when I looked through the forums after encountering a few deaths from that. Hopefully you're aware now if you read up to this point. EDIT 2: Reached Lv20. Only played it out of spite from all the "skill issue" reactions. Still want that thing gone.

I wanted to like this game, but it didn't click. It's an especially hard-to-parse twin-stick, and it has a "lose an upgrade when hit" mechanic that's not too unusual for the genre but it is never a mechanic I've liked. I think the best things the game has going for it are that it's short and you can choose which wave to fight, but even with that I find one mistake snowballs into failure too fast, especially for something so visually chaotic. Hard to want to boot it up when so many other arcade games and roguelikes exist.

[i]Evil Egg’s[i] visual style is initially the thing that drew me in. On the store page the game looked crazy. In some screenshots i couldn’t even find the player avatar. The flashing, bright and hostile visuals were paired with a myteriuos game description. A story that compells me before it even started? This one must surely be a winner. But, alas, it wasn’t meant to be. Once i saw just how unreadable the game can get, i knew i wouldn’t have much fun with it. Another obstacle is how punishing it is. Upon getting hit you lose not only a heart, but also an upgrade. This makes it extremely difficult to persist, given that it’s difficult to (quite often) even see what hit you. Otherwise the gameplay feels nice. Just fine, nothing remarkable really. Weirdly there’s no music unless you count the droning, ominous sound of the opening screen. A couple of great tracks would go a long way.

A modern take on Robotron with some well-balanced roguelike elements. Also a must-play, albeit not for the photosensitive or challenge-averse. If you're neither, this is simply one of those games that you need to go into and complete blind. Don't look anything up, even after you fail a bunch of times or make it to a certain point. Keep the few surprises as they are. The game is a trip. At some points, you will likely find yourself in awe, unable to explain what you're seeing while still being completely engrossed. It is an audial and visual assault that is masterfully balanced and clear. Best played in a dark room with a pair of earbuds or headphones. 40-somethings in particular will feel right at home with the aesthetic. There is a ton of replayability in what's offered. There are even leaderboards. I'm thankful to have had this pop up in a store feed that I so rarely check in the first place. A very nice surprise. It's free, incredibly. You have nothing to lose.

Devil Daggers, Hyper Demon, Xenotilt Pinball, I am your beast, ULTRAKILL and now Evil Egg? People keep making these games that let you be super precise while zoning out to perceive the whole screen at once. So much is going on visually while the design language gives you everything you need to know to stay alive and keep going. It has a high score leaderboard, incredibly punchy sound FX (Also the most brooding drone in the background to always keep you tense), really responsive controls and a tight loop. I know there's some secrets to this game based on some of the things I have seen so far. Evil Egg. Welcome to the "Increases my heartrate and makes me get mad at only myself for screwing up" club. $0.00 for you to try.

This is a Great Robotron: 2084 / Smash T.V. style game, but there's only one major issue with it. The game doesn't lie when it warns you about it having a photosensitivity warning and strobing lights. I don't even have photosensitivity and this becomes way too much even for me in the more difficult rooms, it's to such an extreme degree that you can't even see which way to dodge due to all the flashing lights and overly saturaded colors. The thing is, you'll die to not being able to see what's going on, not directly due to the enemies. There's a great game here, but I sadly have to give it a negative review seeing as you can't turn the worst effects off or at least tone it down.
